subdomain: 4.4 Diagnose system issues (prompt failure, hallucinations, model mismatch)

en.question: A draft-invoice assistant applies the wrong customer's discount ceiling. Retrieved policy and the validated request both identify customer B's 8% ceiling. The saved compiled system prompt instead inserts customer A's 15% ceiling from the template assembler's mutable cached binding, and the output follows 15%. What should the first targeted correction address?

options.text: Increase retrieval depth and retain the compiled system prompt, testing whether additional policy passages outweigh its ceiling.
options.note: The correct policy is already retrieved. Adding lower-trust evidence does not repair the assembler that puts the wrong customer's value into trusted instructions.

options.text: Add more invoice demonstrations to the template while retaining the cached customer binding across requests.
options.note: Examples leave the wrong request-specific instruction in place. They do not fix the established association between customer identity and the compiled ceiling.

options.text: Bind policy values from each validated request; inspect compiled prompts and test alternating-customer cases.
options.note: The trace locates the defect in application prompt assembly. Request-scoped binding and alternating-customer regressions target stale substitutions rather than attributing compliance with the supplied wrong ceiling to model capability.

options.text: Compare stronger generation models using identical compiled prompts and choose the one that most often ignores the 15% instruction.
options.note: The application still sends the wrong trusted policy value. Choosing a model that sometimes disregards it would mask the integration defect rather than establish correct per-customer instructions.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Demystifying evals for AI agents
